This project tackles the issue with a blockchain-based solution votes are recorded across a decentralized network, making them tamper-proof and transparent. Each vote is time-stamped and linked to the previous one, creating an unalterable record. Anyone can verify the results without compromising voter anonymity. The system's trust comes from its code, not a central authority, giving power back to the voters.

This project is set out to craft and launch a safe E-voting app, It runs on blockchain tech. The goal stays clear, wipe out election fraud and bring back trust in the vote count. Picture votes locked in a digital chain no one can tamper with it. Each step shows up for all to see. No central boss holds the keys, Voters pick in peace, Results flows fast and true.

A decentralized ledger system between nodes in a peer-to-peer network that is ordered in a chronological manner and secured using cryptography.
A smart contract is a computerized transaction protocol that will automatically execute the terms of a contract (Szabo, 1994).
This is a feature of data that makes it impossible to change, edit, or delete after a timestamp is assigned to the data, thereby appending it to a chain.
A DApp is an application that runs on a decentralized network, like a blockchain, rather than a central server. It allows for peer-to-peer interactions without intermediaries. (Buterin, 2014)
The EVM is a runtime environment for executing smart contracts on the Ethereum blockchain. It provides a sandboxed environment for executing bytecode. (Ethereum Foundation, n.d.).
Gas is a unit of measurement for the computational effort required to execute a transaction or run a smart contract on the Ethereum network. (Ethereum Foundation, n.d.).
A node is a computer connected to a blockchain network that helps validate transactions and maintain the integrity of the network. (Nakamoto, 2008).
PKI is a system that uses public-private key pairs to authenticate and verify identities. In this project, it's used for secure voter authentication. (Diffie & Hellman, 1976).
A zero-knowledge proof is a cryptographic technique that allows one party to prove the validity of a statement without revealing any underlying information. (Goldwasser et al., 1985).
BFT is a measure of a system's ability to resist failures or malicious behavior from nodes in a distributed network. (Lamport et al., 1982).
An immutable ledger is a record-keeping system where transactions, once recorded, cannot be altered or deleted. (Swan, 2015).

The foundation of the study is based on the theory of Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT). BFT is a theory that identifies a computing system that is able to function correctly despite the failure or malicious conduct of certain nodes (Lamport, Shostak, & Pease, 1982). Moreover, the Decentralized Application (DApp) Model is used to create a bridge that connects the conventional web frontend to the backend of the blockchain technology.
